title: Concentration Terms
syllabus: Solutions and concentration expressions; Mass percentage (% w/w), volume percentage (% v/v), and mass by volume percentage (% w/v); Parts per million (ppm); Mole fraction; Molarity (M) and effect of temperature; Molality (m) and temperature independence; Normality (N) and n-factor (valency factor); Interconversions between concentration terms (Molarity to Molality, % w/w to Molarity); Dilution law and mixing of non-reacting solutions

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An aqueous solution of glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$, molar mass $= 180\text{ g/mol}$) is labelled as $10\%\text{ (w/w)}$. If the density of the solution is $1.2\text{ g/mL}$, the molarity of the solution is:
questions.solution:
Consider $100\text{ g}$ of the solution.
Mass of glucose (solute) $= 10\text{ g}$.
Moles of glucose $= \frac{10}{180} = \frac{1}{18}\text{ mol}$.
Volume of solution:
$$V = \frac{\text{Mass of solution}}{\text{Density}} = \frac{100\text{ g}}{1.2\text{ g/mL}} = \frac{100}{1.2}\text{ mL} = \frac{100}{1200}\text{ L} = \frac{1}{12}\text{ L}$$
Molarity ($M$):
$$M = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution (in L)}} = \frac{1/18}{1/12} = \frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.67\text{ M}$$
Alternatively, using the direct formula:
$$M = \frac{(\%\text{ w/w}) \times d \times 10}{M_{\text{solute}}} = \frac{10 \times 1.2 \times 10}{180} = \frac{120}{180} = 0.67\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Which of the following concentration terms is/are temperature independent?
questions.solution:
Concentration terms that depend strictly on masses of components (solute and solvent) do not change with temperature, because mass is temperature-independent.
- Molality ($m = \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}}$) is temperature independent.
- Mole fraction ($X_A = \frac{n_A}{n_A + n_B}$) is temperature independent.
- Mass percentage (% w/w) and ppm are also temperature independent.
In contrast, Molarity, Normality, and % (v/v) involve the volume of the solution, which expands or contracts with temperature variations.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The mole fraction of a solute in an aqueous solution is $0.1$. The molality of this solution is approximately:
questions.solution:
Let total moles in the solution be $1\text{ mol}$.
- Moles of solute ($n_{\text{solute}}$) $= 0.1\text{ mol}$
- Moles of solvent (water, $n_{\text{solvent}}$) $= 1 - 0.1 = 0.9\text{ mol}$

Mass of solvent (water, molar mass $= 18\text{ g/mol}$):
$$W_{\text{solvent}} = 0.9 \times 18 = 16.2\text{ g} = 0.0162\text{ kg}$$
Molality ($m$):
$$m = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{W_{\text{solvent}}(\text{in kg})} = \frac{0.1}{0.0162} = \frac{100}{16.2} \approx 6.17\text{ m}$$
Alternatively, using the relation $m = \frac{X_{\text{solute}} \times 1000}{(1 - X_{\text{solute}}) M_{\text{solvent}}}$:
$$m = \frac{0.1 \times 1000}{0.9 \times 18} = \frac{100}{16.2} = 6.17\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If $200\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ is mixed with $300\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the normality of the resulting acidic mixture is:
questions.solution:
Find the normality of each acid:
- For $\text{HCl}$: $n$-factor $= 1 \implies N_1 = M_1 \times 1 = 0.2\text{ N}$.
$$\text{Milli-equivalents of HCl} = N_1 V_1 = 0.2 \times 200 = 40\text{ meq}$$
- For $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: $n$-factor $= 2 \implies N_2 = M_2 \times 2 = 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2\text{ N}$.
$$\text{Milli-equivalents of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = N_2 V_2 = 0.2 \times 300 = 60\text{ meq}$$

Total milli-equivalents of $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{Total meq} = 40 + 60 = 100\text{ meq}$$
Total volume of mixture:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 200 + 300 = 500\text{ mL}$$
Normality of mixture:
$$N_{\text{mix}} = \frac{\text{Total meq}}{V_{\text{total}}} = \frac{100}{500} = 0.20\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An aqueous solution of ethanol has a density of $1.025\text{ g/mL}$ and is $2.05\text{ M}$. The molality of the solution is: (Molar mass of ethanol $= 46\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $1\text{ L}$ ($1000\text{ mL}$) of the solution:
- Moles of ethanol $= 2.05\text{ mol}$
- Mass of ethanol $= 2.05 \times 46 = 94.3\text{ g}$
- Mass of $1000\text{ mL}$ of solution $= 1000 \times 1.025 = 1025\text{ g}$
- Mass of solvent (water) $= 1025 - 94.3 = 930.7\text{ g} = 0.9307\text{ kg}$

Molality ($m$):
$$m = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \frac{2.05}{0.9307} \approx 2.20\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] What volume of water must be added to $250\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M } \text{NaOH}$ solution to make it a $0.1\text{ M}$ solution?
questions.solution:
Using the dilution formula:
$$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$$
Here $M_1 = 0.5\text{ M}$, $V_1 = 250\text{ mL}$, and $M_2 = 0.1\text{ M}$:
$$0.5 \times 250 = 0.1 \times V_2$$
$$125 = 0.1 V_2 \implies V_2 = \frac{125}{0.1} = 1250\text{ mL}$$
Volume of water to be added:
$$V_{\text{added}} = V_2 - V_1 = 1250 - 250 = 1000\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A sample of drinking water was found to be severely contaminated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$), supposed to be a carcinogen. The level of contamination was $15\text{ ppm}$ (by mass). The percentage by mass is:
questions.solution:
By definition:
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 10^6$$
$$\%\text{ by mass} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 100$$
Therefore:
$$\%\text{ by mass} = \frac{\text{ppm}}{10^4} = \frac{15}{10^4} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\%$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The molarity of a $98\%\text{ (w/w) } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution with density $1.80\text{ g/mL}$ is: (Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the relation between molarity, density, and mass percentage:
$$M = \frac{x \times d \times 10}{M_{\text{solute}}}$$
where $x = 98$, $d = 1.80\text{ g/mL}$, and $M_{\text{solute}} = 98\text{ g/mol}$:
$$M = \frac{98 \times 1.80 \times 10}{98} = 18.0\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The normality of $0.3\text{ M } \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ (phosphorous acid) solution is:
questions.solution:
Phosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$) is a dibasic acid because it has two ionizable $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds and one non-ionizable $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bond.
Its basicity ($n$-factor) is $2$.
$$\text{Normality} = \text{Molarity} \times n\text{-factor} = 0.3\text{ M} \times 2 = 0.6\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] $500\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{NaCl}$ solution is mixed with $500\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M } \text{CaCl}_2$ solution. The molarity of chloride ions in the resulting solution is:
questions.solution:
1. Moles of $\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{NaCl}$:
$$\text{Molar concentration of } \text{Cl}^- = 0.1\text{ M}$$
$$\text{Millimoles of } \text{Cl}^- = 500 \times 0.1 = 50\text{ mmol}$$
2. Moles of $\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{CaCl}_2$:
Each mole of $\text{CaCl}_2$ yields $2\text{ moles of } \text{Cl}^-$.
$$\text{Concentration of } \text{Cl}^- = 2 \times 0.2 = 0.4\text{ M}$$
$$\text{Millimoles of } \text{Cl}^- = 500 \times 0.4 = 200\text{ mmol}$$
3. Total millimoles of $\text{Cl}^- = 50 + 200 = 250\text{ mmol}$.
Total volume $= 500 + 500 = 1000\text{ mL} = 1\text{ L}$.
$$\text{Molarity of } \text{Cl}^- = \frac{250\text{ mmol}}{1000\text{ mL}} = 0.25\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A solution is prepared by dissolving $24.5\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in water to make $250\text{ mL}$ of solution. The normality of this solution is:
questions.solution:
Equivalent mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = \frac{\text{Molar mass}}{n\text{-factor}} = \frac{98}{2} = 49\text{ g/eq}$.
Number of equivalents:
$$\text{Equivalents} = \frac{24.5\text{ g}}{49\text{ g/eq}} = 0.5\text{ eq}$$
Volume of solution in liters:
$$V = \frac{250\text{ mL}}{1000} = 0.25\text{ L}$$
Normality:
$$N = \frac{0.5\text{ eq}}{0.25\text{ L}} = 2.0\text{ N}$$

questions.question: If the mole fraction of urea in an aqueous solution is $0.05$, the percentage by mass of urea in the solution is: (Molar masses: Urea $= 60\text{ g/mol}$, Water $= 18\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
In $1\text{ mole}$ of solution:
- Moles of urea $= 0.05\text{ mol}$
- Moles of water $= 1 - 0.05 = 0.95\text{ mol}$

Masses:
- $\text{Mass of urea} = 0.05 \times 60 = 3.0\text{ g}$
- $\text{Mass of water} = 0.95 \times 18 = 17.1\text{ g}$
- $\text{Total mass of solution} = 3.0 + 17.1 = 20.1\text{ g}$

Percentage by mass:
$$\%\text{ urea} = \frac{3.0}{20.1} \times 100 \approx 14.92\% \approx 14.9\%$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.6\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ and $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.4\text{ M } \text{NaOH}$ are mixed together. The resulting solution is:
questions.solution:
Neutralization reaction:
$$\text{HCl} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Millimoles of reactants:
- $\text{Millimoles of } \text{H}^+ = 100 \times 0.6 = 60\text{ mmol}$
- $\text{Millimoles of } \text{OH}^- = 100 \times 0.4 = 40\text{ mmol}$

Remaining millimoles of $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{Excess } \text{H}^+ = 60 - 40 = 20\text{ mmol}$$
Total volume:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 100 + 100 = 200\text{ mL}$$
Concentration of $\text{H}^+$:
$$[\text{H}^+] = \frac{20\text{ mmol}}{200\text{ mL}} = 0.1\text{ M}$$
Hence, the solution is acidic with $[\text{H}^+] = 0.1\text{ M}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An aqueous solution of $\text{NaOH}$ is labelled $10\%\text{ (w/v)}$. If the density of the solution is $1.05\text{ g/mL}$, the percentage by mass (% w/w) of $\text{NaOH}$ is:
questions.solution:
By definition, $10\%\text{ (w/v)}$ means $10\text{ g of NaOH}$ is present in $100\text{ mL of solution}$.
Mass of $100\text{ mL}$ of solution:
$$\text{Mass} = \text{Volume} \times d = 100\text{ mL} \times 1.05\text{ g/mL} = 105\text{ g}$$
Percentage by mass (% w/w):
$$\%\text{ (w/w)} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 100 = \frac{10}{105} \times 100 = \frac{1000}{105} \approx 9.52\%$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A $1.0\text{ molal}$ aqueous solution of a non-electrolyte solute has a mole fraction of solute equal to:
questions.solution:
A $1.0\text{ molal}$ solution contains $1\text{ mole of solute}$ in $1000\text{ g of water}$.
Moles of water:
$$n_{\text{water}} = \frac{1000\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 55.55\text{ mol}$$
Mole fraction of solute:
$$X_{\text{solute}} = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solute}} + n_{\text{water}}} = \frac{1}{1 + 55.55} = \frac{1}{56.55} \approx 0.0177$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If $V_1\text{ mL}$ of $M_1\text{ molar}$ solution is mixed with $V_2\text{ mL}$ of $M_2\text{ molar}$ solution of the same non-reacting substance, the molarity of the mixture is given by:
questions.solution:
Total millimoles of the solute present in the mixture:
$$\text{Total mmol} = M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2$$
Assuming volumes are additive, total volume:
$$V_{\text{total}} = V_1 + V_2$$
By definition of molarity:
$$M_{\text{mix}} = \frac{\text{Total mmol}}{\text{Total volume (in mL)}} = \frac{M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2}{V_1 + V_2}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] What is the molarity of pure liquid water? (Density of water $= 1.00\text{ g/mL}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $1\text{ L}$ ($1000\text{ mL}$) of pure water:
$$\text{Mass of } 1000\text{ mL of water} = 1000\text{ mL} \times 1.00\text{ g/mL} = 1000\text{ g}$$
Molar mass of water $= 18.015\text{ g/mol} \approx 18\text{ g/mol}$.
Number of moles in $1\text{ L}$:
$$n = \frac{1000\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} \approx 55.556\text{ mol}$$
$$\text{Molarity} = \frac{55.556\text{ mol}}{1\text{ L}} \approx 55.56\text{ M}$$

questions.question: The $n$-factor of potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) when it acts as an oxidizing agent in acidic medium is:
questions.solution:
In acidic medium, permanganate ion undergoes reduction according to the half-reaction:
$$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
The oxidation state of manganese changes from $+7$ to $+2$.
Change in oxidation state per molecule $= 7 - 2 = 5$.
Therefore, the $n$-factor is $5$, and its equivalent mass in acidic medium is $\frac{M}{5}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] If the solubility of a gas in water is $0.002\text{ g/L}$, its concentration in parts per million (ppm) is: (Density of water $= 1\text{ g/mL}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of $1\text{ L of water} = 1000\text{ g}$.
Mass of dissolved gas in $1\text{ L} = 0.002\text{ g}$.
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 10^6$$
Since the solution is extremely dilute, mass of solution $\approx 1000\text{ g}$:
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{0.002\text{ g}}{1000\text{ g}} \times 10^6 = 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^6 = 2\text{ ppm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] To prepare $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution from crystalline $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (washing soda), the mass of crystals required is: (Molar mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} = 286\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ required:
$$n = M \times V(\text{in L}) = 0.1\text{ M} \times 0.1\text{ L} = 0.01\text{ mol}$$
Each mole of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is provided by $1\text{ mole of } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Mass of washing soda crystals needed:
$$\text{Mass} = 0.01\text{ mol} \times 286\text{ g/mol} = 2.86\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A solution of glucose in water has a molality of $2.0\text{ m}$. Find the mole fraction of glucose in the solution (rounded to three decimal places).
questions.solution:
$2.0\text{ m}$ solution contains $2.0\text{ moles of glucose}$ in $1000\text{ g of water}$.
Moles of water $= \frac{1000}{18} = 55.55\text{ mol}$.
Mole fraction of glucose:
$$X = \frac{2.0}{2.0 + 55.55} = \frac{2.0}{57.55} \approx 0.03475 \approx 0.035$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the molarity of a solution obtained by mixing $750\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ with $250\text{ mL}$ of $2.0\text{ M } \text{HCl}$.
questions.solution:
Total millimoles of $\text{HCl}$:
$$\text{Total mmol} = (750 \times 0.5) + (250 \times 2.0) = 375 + 500 = 875\text{ mmol}$$
Total volume:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 750 + 250 = 1000\text{ mL}$$
Molarity of mixture:
$$M = \frac{875\text{ mmol}}{1000\text{ mL}} = 0.875\text{ M} \approx 0.88\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] What volume (in mL) of $12\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ is required to prepare $600\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ solution?
questions.solution:
Using the dilution equation:
$$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$$
$$12 \times V_1 = 0.2 \times 600$$
$$12 V_1 = 120 \implies V_1 = 10.0\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If $4.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ is dissolved in $250\text{ mL}$ of water, find the molarity of the resulting solution. (Molar mass of $\text{NaOH} = 40\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Moles of $\text{NaOH} = \frac{4.0\text{ g}}{40\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$.
Volume of solution $= 250\text{ mL} = 0.25\text{ L}$.
Molarity:
$$M = \frac{0.1\text{ mol}}{0.25\text{ L}} = 0.4\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In an oxidation-reduction reaction, $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ in acidic medium accepts $6\text{ moles of electrons}$ to form $\text{Cr}^{3+}$. If the molarity of the $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution is $0.25\text{ M}$, find its normality.
questions.solution:
The reduction half-reaction in acidic medium is:
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
The $n$-factor (valency factor) is $6$ electrons per mole.
$$\text{Normality} = \text{Molarity} \times n\text{-factor} = 0.25 \times 6 = 1.5\text{ N}$$
